author: Zeno Ren
probe_model_choice: databricks-claude-opus-5 rather than opus-5-5, which is intermittently capacity-limited upstream and caused the 2026-10-10 rollback when used as a mandatory gate

two_step_release.why: the panel password has to reach the pod as an env var, and the release tool's plan deep-copies the live pod template — so the env must be in place before planning, which is itself a rollout

step_1.method: kubectl patch --type=json, after a server-side dry-run diff

step_2.action: release tool plan + submit to db8845a

secret_handling.change: added one key, LB_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, by merge patch
secret_handling.why_this_secret: its name is already in the controller Role's secrets.resourceNames, so no RBAC change was needed — the 2026-10-14 preflight 403 was exactly a missing resourceNames entry
secret_handling.password_set_by: operator, in their own terminal; the value never passed through the assistant
secret_handling.note: Kubernetes Secret data is base64, not encryption, so the password is recoverable by anyone with read access to the namespace — the same trust boundary as LB_CREDENTIAL_KEY

login_verified_live.method: issued from inside the pod against the public URL, so the password never left the cluster
login_verified_live.secure_present: yes — the public ingress terminates TLS, so X-Forwarded-Proto is https

schema_unchanged: model_copilot_account already existed from the previous release; this batch creates no table and alters no column

build.controller_rebuild_not_needed: operations/ and the APP_FILES set are unchanged since 7229327

operator_errors_this_run: The private release notes said this Deployment is not apply-managed and prescribed a JSON patch. It IS apply-managed. The prescribed command was right but the stated reason was wrong, and acting on the reason would have been worse: its last-applied-configuration is badly stale (image 2f6fa30-full, env []), so the 'rebuild from last-applied and apply' technique used on the Role two days earlier would have rolled the image back to an ancient tag, wiped every env var, and reset the probes. Caught by diffing last-applied against live before touching anything.
The password-setting command was written with bash's `read -rsp`; this shell is zsh, where -p means 'read from coprocess' and the command fails. Replaced with a stty form verified under both shells.

The secret-verification command used `-o jsonpath='{range $k,$v := .data}…'`, which this kubectl silently prints as empty for a map — it briefly looked as though the Secret had no keys at all. `kubectl describe secret` is the right tool: it reports byte counts and no values.
verification_caveat: A Secret's byte count is not its character count, and the gateway's minimum is on characters. 13 bytes here happened to be 13 ASCII characters; a multi-byte password of the same byte length could have been under the floor and silently treated as unconfigured. Checked explicitly against the gateway's own _panel_password().
